segments.t: Kostya volunteers to bring the champagne to room 202 himself so he can film Louis and Polina together as proof for Nastya. Meanwhile, Senya and Fedya finish feeding their model for the third time and eagerly await their promised reward.

Только смотри не делай как Луи!

Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Давай я сам принесу вам шампанское.
'Let me bring you the champagne myself.' Kostya presents a serious note straight away, leaning on "davay" ("let's") before closing the thought with "prinesu" ("I will bring").
Принесёшь прямо в номер, это отлично!

'You will bring it right to the room, that is great!' Louis chooses a candid footing toward Senya, anchoring the Russian line on "prinesyosh" ("to bring") and "pryamo" ("right, just") without extra filler.
Запомни, у нас двести второй номер.
'Remember, we have room two hundred and two.' Louis favors a lively angle for Kostya, building the phrase around "zapomni" ("remember") and "vtoroy" ("second") for a crisp, natural delivery.
Большое спасибо тебе за помощь, Костя.
'Thank you very much for your help, Kostya.' Louis sets a playful position at this moment, combining "bolshoye" ("big, very much") and "spasibo" ("thank you") so the key meaning lands right away.
Саша, присмотри пока за моим баром.
'Sasha, watch my bar for now.' Kostya displays a direct course in the scene, pairing "prismotri" ("supervision") with "poka" ("bye") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
Только смотри не делай как Луи!
'Just mind you do not do like Louis!' Kostya chooses a firm view in the room, building the phrase around "tolko" ("only") and "smotri" ("look") for a crisp, natural delivery.
Скажи, тебе было сегодня очень вкусно?
'Tell us, was it very tasty for you today?' Senya probes promptly as the talk turns, anchoring the Russian line on "skazhi" ("say") and "bylo" ("was") without extra filler.
Молодцы, вы честно заслужили свою награду.

'Well done, you honestly earned your reward.' Senya shows a resolute direction in front of Louis, joining "molodtsy" ("well done, good person") to "chestno" ("honestly") so every word pulls its weight.
Ну давай уже скорее награждай нас!

'Well come on and reward us quickly already!' Senya chooses an unhurried tone during the exchange, building the phrase around "davay" ("let's") and "uzhe" ("already, now") for a crisp, natural delivery.
Мы честно кормили тебя два дня.
'We honestly fed you for two days.' Senya holds a firm bearing beside Louis, putting "chestno" ("honestly") alongside "kormili" ("to feed") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
Хорошо, ребята, закройте пока свои глаза.
'Alright, guys, close your eyes for now.' Louis conveys a steady posture in front of Kostya, leaning on "khorosho" ("good, fine") before closing the thought with "rebyata" ("the boys, the lads").
Мы уже закрыли глаза и ждём.

'We have already closed our eyes and are waiting.' Senya picks a playful direction in this beat, building the phrase around "uzhe" ("already, now") and "zakryli" ("to close, to shut") for a crisp, natural delivery.
